issues.legal_issue: A mining-lease renewal is governed by the law and conditions in force at renewal, allowing the state to impose a captive-use condition where no applicable provision requires renewal on the original terms.
material_facts: The lease was granted before the central government approved the state’s proposal to include conditions requiring industrial use of bauxite, including establishment of a captive plant.
The lease terms and governing law did not require renewal on the same terms and conditions as the original grant.
The state sought to impose the captive-plant condition when the mining lease was renewed.
issues.conclusion: The state had power at renewal to impose a condition requiring establishment of a captive plant.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rule 27(3) of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, the state could include conditions for which the central government had given its approval. A renewal is a fresh grant governed by the law in force at the time of renewal, unless the lease or governing law provides for renewal on the original terms. The Court relied on Gajraj Singh v. State Transport Appellate Tribunal, which discusses the distinction between renewal and extension drawn in Provash Chandra Dalui v. Biswanath Banerjee and refers to State of M.P. v. Krishnadas Tikaram.

rule.if: mining_lease_renewal and central_permission_for_lease_conditions and not original_terms_mandated_on_renewal

predicates.mining_lease_renewal: The proceeding concerns renewal of a mining lease.
predicates.central_permission_for_lease_conditions: The central government approved the state’s proposal to include conditions governing leaseholders’ use of the mineral.
predicates.original_terms_mandated_on_renewal: The lease or governing law requires the renewal to be granted on the original terms and conditions.
predicates.state_may_impose_captive_use_condition_a: The state may impose a condition requiring captive industrial use when renewing the mining lease.

issues.definition: When a mining lease is being renewed, the state may impose a captive-use condition if the central government approved lease conditions and renewal on the original terms is not mandated.

issues.legal_issue: Central approval for lease conditions in an area released from reservation applies to a mine in that area even if its existing lease was not affected by the original reservation.
material_facts: The mine was in a district whose mineral areas were later released from reservation after central approval for including conditions on leaseholders.
The existing lease predated that approval, and the original reservation had not affected the mine.
The state sought to apply the approved lease conditions at renewal.
issues.conclusion: The central government’s approval for including conditions applied to the existing lease; the fact that the mine had not been affected by the original reservation did not exclude it.
issues.legal_principle: The central government’s approval under Rule 27(3) of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 extended to lease conditions for mines in the districts covered by the release from reservation. After that approval, fresh grants and renewals of existing leases stood on the same footing; excluding an existing lease merely because it had not been affected by the original reservation would be impermissible.

rule.if: mining_lease_renewal_dispute and central_permission_for_lease_conditions and mine_in_area_covered_by_permission and existing_lease_unaffected_by_original_reservation

predicates.mining_lease_renewal_dispute: The dispute concerns applying lease conditions when an existing mining lease is renewed.
predicates.central_permission_for_lease_conditions: The central government approved the state’s proposal to include conditions for leaseholders in the relevant mineral area.
predicates.mine_in_area_covered_by_permission: The mine is in a district or area covered by that approval.
predicates.existing_lease_unaffected_by_original_re: The existing lease was not affected by the earlier reservation of the area.
predicates.central_permission_conditions_apply_to_e: The approved conditions may apply to the existing lease notwithstanding that the original reservation did not affect the mine.

issues.definition: Approved lease conditions apply to an existing lease in the covered area when the lease is renewed, even if the mine was unaffected by the original reservation.
